findings.title: "Forgot your password?" control is not keyboard-focusable on the login page
findings.severityRationale: Keyboard-only and assistive-tech users cannot reach the account-recovery path; a mouse workaround is required.
findings.priorityRationale: Blocks a core public flow for a user group; simple fix (use <a>/<button>).
steps: Press Tab repeatedly from the top of the page
Observe focus order: Username/Password -> Login -> 4 social icon links -> OrangeHRM, Inc -> body; 'Forgot your password?' never receives focus
Note the text is also not exposed as a link/button (absent from the page's link and button lists), yet a mouse click navigates to /auth/requestPasswordResetCode
findings.expected: The recovery control is a focusable link or button reachable by Tab and activatable by Enter.
findings.expectedSource: convention: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.actual: Element is clickable by mouse only (EV-004 shows mouse navigation works) but is absent from tab order and from links/buttons (EV-001, EV-003).
findings.impact: Keyboard/screen-reader users cannot start password recovery.
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Confirm with a screen reader (NVDA/VoiceOver) and in Firefox/WebKit.

findings.title: Login page shows raw translation keys and throws uncaught AxiosError when i18n messages API fails
findings.severityRationale: Entire login UI becomes unreadable keys (auth.login, general.username) with no user-facing error or retry; affects all users if the i18n endpoint degrades.
findings.priorityRationale: Requires backend failure to trigger, but impact on that occasion is total for the entry page.
preconditions: GET /web/index.php/core/i18n/messages returns HTTP 500 (simulated in investigator browser only)
steps: Simulate 500 for /core/i18n/messages in the browser session
findings.expected: Fallback to default (English) strings or a clear error with retry; no unhandled exception.
findings.expectedSource: convention: graceful degradation of non-critical dependency / error handling for failed XHR
findings.actual: Visible text: 'auth.login ... general.username general.password auth.login auth.forgot_password?'. Console: pageerror 'AxiosError: fe' (uncaught).
findings.impact: Users see a broken, unlabeled login screen during i18n outages.
findings.scope: Login page (likely all Vue pages that load i18n)
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Check other failure modes (timeout/abort) and reset-password page.

evidence.label: Login page with i18n API returning 500

findings.title: Login/reset forms lack accessible names, page lang and named icon links; validation errors not exposed programmatically
findings.severityRationale: Screen readers announce unnamed fields/links; 'Required' errors are visual only.
findings.priorityRationale: Broad but individually small fixes; no functional block for sighted users.
steps: Username/password inputs rely on placeholder only
<html> has no lang; no <h1>; 4 social icon links have no accessible name
Click Login with empty fields: 'Required' shown but no field reports invalid state
findings.expected: Inputs programmatically labelled, html lang set, icon links have aria-label, invalid fields set aria-invalid/aria-describedby.
findings.actual: As described; same pattern on reset page (EV-005).
findings.impact: Assistive-technology users get poor or missing announcements on the entry pages.
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Full axe + screen-reader audit; check contrast and button focus indicators.

findings.title: HTML pages lack clickjacking protection (no X-Frame-Options, no CSP frame-ancestors); CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval
findings.severityRationale: Header-level indicator only; exploitability (e.g., framing the login page) not demonstrated and framing an unauthenticated login page has limited impact.
findings.expected: X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN or CSP frame-ancestors 'self'; CSP without unsafe-eval.
findings.expectedSource: convention: OWASP Secure Headers Project / OWASP Clickjacking Defense Cheat Sheet
findings.actual: No X-Frame-Options; CSP 'default-src blob: 'self' ... 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'' with no frame-ancestors. Also no Referrer-Policy.
findings.impact: Pages could be framed by third-party sites (clickjacking); CSP gives weak XSS mitigation.
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Safe framing PoC on a local page to confirm browser renders the frame; review authenticated pages.

findings.title: Server header discloses nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu) and HSTS is missing on REST API / error responses
findings.severityRationale: Information disclosure and inconsistent transport hardening; no direct exploit shown.
findings.expected: Server version suppressed; Strict-Transport-Security on all HTTPS responses.
findings.expectedSource: convention: OWASP Secure Headers Project / RFC 6797
findings.actual: Server: nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu) on all responses; Strict-Transport-Security present on HTML routes but absent on /api/v2/* and 404 responses.
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Set server_tokens off; add HSTS at nginx level for every location.

findings.title: REST API returns misleading 'Session expired' to never-authenticated clients; unknown API routes return empty HTML 404
findings.severityRationale: Contract/consistency issue affecting API consumers' error handling; access control itself works (401).
findings.priorityRationale: Cosmetic for UI, minor for integrators.
findings.expected: 401 with a message such as 'Unauthorized'/'Authentication required'; unknown API routes return a JSON error body consistent with other API errors.
findings.expectedSource: convention: consistent REST error contract (RFC 9457 problem details style)
findings.actual: 401 {"error":{"status":401,"message":"Session expired"}} for a fresh client; 404 text/html with empty body for unknown /api/v2 path.
findings.impact: Clients cannot distinguish expiry from missing auth; inconsistent content types complicate error handling.
findings.suggestedFollowUp: Check with authenticated session whether the message differs for real expiry.

limitations: Browsers not installed for this Playwright version: firefox, webkit. Cross-browser checks on them are blocked.
Mission is read-only (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS); create/update/delete behaviour was not exercised through the API tool.
No requirements were recorded; expectations rely on stated conventions, so requirements coverage cannot be computed.
Security checks were limited to safe, non-destructive observations within the authorised scope. The absence of findings in an area is not evidence that it is secure.
No direct database or service-layer access was available unless stated; data-integrity conclusions are based on UI/API observations only.

Read-only scope: login (POST /auth/validate) and reset-password submission (POST) were not exercised, so authentication, invalid-credential messaging, lockout/rate limiting and all post-login modules are untested.
No credentials were supplied as secrets; authenticated API authorization (IDOR, role checks) was not tested.
Chromium only; Firefox and WebKit were unavailable.
No requirements or API documentation were found on in-scope pages; expectations are based on cited conventions (WCAG, OWASP, RFC) rather than product requirements.
API endpoints beyond the observed i18n call were probed by OrangeHRM 5 path convention, not from a published spec, so the endpoint denominator is incomplete.
A keyboard Enter-activation check crashed the investigator connection; the mission was resumed and keyboard reachability was concluded from focus-order capture and DOM verification instead.
Accessibility checks are heuristic; no screen-reader or colour-contrast audit was performed.
The demo is shared and publicly reset, so behaviour may differ from production deployments.
nextInvestigations: With an approved test environment that allows POST, test login with valid and invalid credentials, lockout/rate limiting, session fixation and logout invalidation.
Use authenticated sessions per role (Admin/ESS) to test REST API v2 authorization, pagination and input validation.
Run the i18n fault injection with timeout and abort modes, and on the reset and dashboard pages.
Do a full screen-reader and axe audit, including focus indicators on buttons (the heuristic flagged them) and colour contrast.
Run a cross-browser pass in Firefox and WebKit.
Build a safe local framing proof of concept to judge clickjacking impact on authenticated pages.
